rows.grounds: compound of divya (divine, celestial) and kṛt (maker); epithet of the deity
compound of dina (day) and kṛt (maker); epithet associated with generating the day
from deva (god, shining one); nominative singular with sandhi before following voiced initial
compound of deva (god) and deva (god), expressing supremacy over other gods
compound of divas/div (heaven, sky) and pati (lord, master)

items.question: What creative powers and sovereign statuses are attributed to the deity by these epithets?
premises: The deity is designated as maker of the divine and maker of the day.
The deity is identified both as god and as god of gods.
The deity is named lord of heaven.
items.inference: Together these epithets portray the deity as a supreme cosmic creator and sovereign ruler.
uncertainties: The precise nuance of divyakṛd may range from maker of the divine to producer of celestial phenomena.
items.plain_english: He is the maker of the divine, the maker of the day, the god, the god of gods, and the lord of heaven.
